text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: paging oncall — high rate of GPU driver resets observed across a subset of vGPU hosts (metric spike at 00:12 UTC). Auto-evac triggered for some tenants. tagging @oncall-alex for triage

oncall-alex: on it. seeing flurry of `Xid 79` and `Xid 13` in the kernel logs from `vgpu-host-12` and `vgpu-host-17`. marking high priority.

infra-rita: grabbing NV logs and dmesg. initial glance: repeated ECC corrected events, then `nv-host` resets followed by user container crashes. looks like soft ECC flares, not full hardware panic yet.

ml-sre-james: customer-facing inference jobs reported OOMs and long tail latencies. autoscaler tried to spin more pods but they land on affected hosts and crash. rolling fallback to cpu/backups recommended.

customer-bridge-priya: opening customer bridge for the handful of affected tenants (prod-critical). collecting list of impacted endpoints. we need ETA and mitigation message.

oncall-alex: immediate steps I propose:
- cordon `vgpu-host-12` & `vgpu-host-17`
- drain non-critical pods, evict affected serving replicas
- route incoming requests to Dedicated pool and fallback models (cpu) for impacted customers
- attempt `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service` on hosts after log capture
- if resets persist, hard reboot with node quarantine

eng-sre-sam: +1. I can drive node cordon/drain. running: `kubectl cordon vgpu-host-12 && kubectl drain vgpu-host-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

monitoring-bot: alert summary:
- `gpu.driver.resets` spike: 320 events in 10m (baseline < 2)
- `gpu.ecc.corrected_rate` increased 40x
- `node.evictions` correlated with resets
- top hosts: vgpu-host-12 (210 resets), vgpu-host-17 (85 resets)

infra-rita: collected `dmesg` snippet and nv-host log excerpt:```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (0000:79): 0x00000000, 0x00000000, 0x00000000
[ 12345.679002] NVRM: Xid (0000:13): CPU fault on GPU 0
[ 12346.000111] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 12346.010222] nv-host: nv-host-core: host reset initiated
```
This pattern repeats with short intervals. No ECC uncorrectable yet but correctable count is climbing rapidly.

oncall-alex: good capture. Sam, start drain on both hosts and spin up a CPU fallback pool (ml-sre-james can flip routing). Priya please notify customers: we are evacuating a subset of GPU hosts due to increased driver resets and routing to safe fallback.

ml-sre-james: flipping model routing — enabling `circuit_breaker_gpu_fallback=true` for affected tenant routes and increasing replica counts in cpu-pool. patching canary first. command:```bash
redwoodctl route update --tenant tenant-a --fallback cpu --circuit-breaker enabled
```
Monitoring: latency spike started to subside for tenant-a after toggling.

customer-bridge-priya: messaging draft for customers: "We detected transient GPU host instability affecting inference latency and errors. We're evacuating impacted hosts, routing traffic to safe fallback compute, and will restore GPU capacity after validation. No model data was exposed. We'll update in 30m or on stable restore." happy to send after Alex signs off. :white_check_mark:

oncall-alex: sign off on message. Priya send.

deploy-bot: automated action: created runbook entry #IR-2026-540999 - "vgpu soft ECC resets - evacuation and driver restart". Added playbook steps and owner.

eng-sre-sam: drain in progress: `kubectl drain vgpu-host-12` -> drained 14 pods; `vgpu-host-17` -> drained 7 pods. Observed one daemonset that rescheduled a GPU bound helper, killed it manually.

infra-rita: attempted `systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service` on vgpu-host-12; driver restarted but resets resumed within ~90s. capturing full nv-host trace and will escalate to hw team for deeper diagnostics.

ml-sre-james: because restarts didn't stabilize, switching to quarantine (reboot) plan. proposing rolling reboot of affected hosts with pre-check snapshot: collect nv-host logs, checkpoint KV cache for warmed embeddings before node reboot.

oncall-alex: agree. schedule reboot window ASAP. Sam, coordinate with infra to ensure no mass capacity loss: we have spare capacity in ded and cpu pools.

eng-sre-sam: reboot initiated for vgpu-host-12. running `sudo reboot`. ETA back ~5m.

monitoring-bot: post-evac metrics (10m after cordon/drain):
- `service.error_rate` for affected tenants down from 12% -> 1.8%
- `queued_requests` reduced by 67%
- `gpu.driver.resets` for cluster dropped to 6 events in 10m (was 320)

infra-rita: after reboot, basic health checks pass on vgpu-host-12. nv-host logs show no new Xid 79 for 8m so far. keeping node quarantined for 30m before uncordon.

customer-bridge-priya: customer update sent. initial responses: two customers acknowledged, one asks for RCA and timeline for full GPU restore.

oncall-alex: next actions:
- keep hosts cordoned until stable 30m window
- gather full logs and open HW ticket if Xid/ ECC frequency resurges
- prepare candidate RCA: likely transient ECC correctable burst -> driver reset cascade -> pod OOMs due to process restarts
- follow up with postmortem template after incident declared resolved

eng-sre-sam: will run a post-reboot stress test (small synthetic infer load) on quarantined host to validate stability before returning to traffic.

infra-rita: attaching quick troubleshooting notes for oncall playbook:```
# triage steps
1) verify `nvidia-smi -q` and `dmesg | grep -i xnvm`
2) collect `/var/log/nv-host.log` and `journalctl -u nvidia-driver`
3) if Xid rates > threshold -> cordon + drain -> attempt driver restart -> if resets persist -> reboot -> quarantine 30m
4) escalate to hardware team with nv-host trace and ECC counters
```

oncall-alex: thanks team. keeping thread open for 30m observation window. if stable, we'll start gradual uncordon with canary pods.

customer-bridge-priya: I'll keep customers posted. closing customer bridge once all impacted tenants show healthy metrics.

monitoring-bot: reminder: followup alert scheduled in 30m for final stability check.

eng-sre-sam: vgpu-host-12 stress test looks good so far (5m synthetic run). preparing to uncordon tomorrow if continued green.

oncall-alex: incident status: mitigated -> evacuations and fallbacks reduced user impact, hosts quarantined and rebooted. will open full incident postmortem with timelines and telemetry. thanks all. :thumbsup:
